transcript: In the latter half of the 18th century, an event began in Britain that would transform society and the economy from its foundation. It was the dawn of the industrial revolution The steam engine improved by James Watt transformed the very concept of power Manufacturing, which had until then depended on rivers or on horses Could now run 24 hours a day on the power of coal and machines In Manchester and Liverpool, huge cotton textile factories were built one after another People who had until then worked the land in the countryside Moved into the urban centres in search of work Urbanisation advanced rapidly during this time But the labour conditions in the factories was terrible Work days of more than 12 hours, low wages and children Forced to work in the mines and the factories Child labour was the dark side of the society of that age After the middle of the 19th century, workers began to organize unions and to strike for better treatment through the efforts of social reformers. Laws limiting child labour were passed one after another. The Industrial Revolution greatly raised living standards and the average life span of humanity. At the same time it brought deep gaps between rich and poor and serious environmental pollution. Our society today still lies on the path of the transformation That the revolution began
